forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces a number for 'you'; Jesus spoke this to groups, and the same plural form is used in 170:1.13 and 170:2.24.
The prayer speaks to God as Father, one person; tú per the Spanish rules.
The text speaks to the reader; the Spanish rules ask for the plural ustedes.

forcedChoices.choice: impersonal «al prójimo como a uno mismo»
forcedChoices.reason: A general maxim; the impersonal form reads better than ustedes and keeps the general sense.
Here 'actual' is the plain word (genuine, as he taught them), not the philosophical term 'en acto' of the glossary.

forcedChoices.choice: «experiencia definida y real» for 'definite and actual experience'
forcedChoices.reason: Plain sense of 'actual'; 'en acto' would add a philosophical sense not intended.

forcedChoices.choice: «el ideal que él tenía» for 'his ideal'
